stemMarkdown: Find the difference (in Rs.) between the compound interest and the simple interest on Rs. 16000 at 12% per annum for 2 years. (Round to 2 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: CI: the amount after 2 years is $20070.40$, so CI $= 4070.40$. SI $= \dfrac{16000 \times 12 \times 2}{100} = 3840.00$. The difference is $230.4$.
altSolutionMarkdown: For 2 years the gap is always the interest earned on the first year's interest: $P\left(\dfrac{R}{100}\right)^2 = 16000 \times \left(\dfrac{12}{100}\right)^2 = 230.4$.
